fixture.text_transport: HF decode and roundtrip checked in benchmark; prior reconstructed GGUF tokenizer proof matches all12 current fixture token-ID hashes exactly.

same_checkpoint.files: Both commands use the same local four GGUF shards. llama points at shard1 and automatically opens the rest. No native quant4 or MTP comparison is included.

unchanged_runtime_precision_disclosure: Same GGUF source does not mean identical runtime arithmetic: mistral.rs selects BF16 activations and loads F32 dense projections as BF16; llama retains its implementation and F32 dense storage. This predates the paired optimization and must remain disclosed.
other_limits: Greedy outputs differ across engines; this is fixed-prompt serving rather than identical teacher-forced routing.
Prompt throughput is prompt_tokens/TTFT, including first-token work and serving overhead.
mistral.rs additionally loads an unused multimodal projector for these text requests.
This is one GB10 and three measured requests per length, not a broad hardware or model-quality claim.
memory_capture: bench_c1_with_memory.py records existing /metrics responses and /proc/meminfo outside TTFT/decode timing; it adds no HTTP requests or cache advice.
fresh_control_script: run_llama_verify.py preserves command except chunk limits, validates fixture/counts, runs full prewarm then measured sweep, checks loaded binary/library hashes and compiler overlap, and shuts down each server.
comparison_rule: Use the maximum llama median per prompt length and metric across historical/fresh512 and8192. A matched8192 table can be separate. Current compare_paired.py prefill uses only historical8192 and is provisional.
